title: The normalization of a domain of finite type over Z is finite
statement: Let $A$ be an integral domain which is generated as a ring by finitely many elements, i.e. $\mathbf Z\to A$ is of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], with field of fractions $K$, and let $A'=\{x\in K: x$ is a root of a monic polynomial with coefficients in $A\}$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $K$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Then $A'$ is a finitely generated $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module].

source.place: Algebra, Proposition Tag 0335 (proposition-ubiquity-nagata), items (3) and (5): Z and rings of finite type over Z are Nagata, in particular universally Japanese; Definition Tag 032R (definition-nagata (1): universally Japanese means every domain of finite type over the ring is N-2) and Definition Tag 032F (definition-N: N-2 with the trivial extension L = K gives N-1, i.e. the integral closure in K is finite). Used in the proof of Lemma Tag 033C (lemma-normal-goes-up): 'As R_0 is a Nagata domain we see that its integral closure R_0' is finite over R_0'

proof.text: *$\mathbf Z$ is a Nagata ring* [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring] (Proposition 0335 (3)). $\mathbf Z$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], since every ideal is $n\mathbf Z$ for some $n\ge0$ (division with remainder by the least positive element). Its prime ideals are $(p)$ for primes $p$ and $(0)$; we show each $\mathbf Z/\mathfrak p$ is N-2 [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain]. (a) $\mathfrak p=(p)$: $\mathbf Z/(p)=\mathbf F_p$ is a field, its own fraction field. For a finite extension $L/\mathbf F_p$ [def-pc-field-extension] every $y\in L$ is algebraic over $\mathbf F_p$ (the powers $1,y,\dots,y^{d}$, $d=\dim L$, are linearly dependent), and dividing a nonzero polynomial relation by its leading coefficient gives a monic one, so $y$ is integral over $\mathbf F_p$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]; the integral closure of $\mathbf F_p$ in $L$ is $L$, which is a finitely generated $\mathbf F_p$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] since $\dim_{\mathbf F_p}L<\infty$. (b) $\mathfrak p=(0)$: $\mathbf Z$ is a normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]: if $x=a/b\in\mathbf Q$ with $\gcd(a,b)=1$, $b>0$, satisfies $x^n+c_{n-1}x^{n-1}+\dots+c_0=0$ with $c_i\in\mathbf Z$, multiplying by $b^n$ gives $a^n=-b(c_{n-1}a^{n-1}+\dots+c_0b^{n-1})$, so every prime factor of $b$ divides $a$, hence $b=1$ and $x\in\mathbf Z$. Let $L/\mathbf Q$ be a finite extension. As $\mathbf Q$ has characteristic $0$, $L/\mathbf Q$ is separable by [lem-weil-pbc-char-zero-field-extension-separable]; since $L/\mathbf Q$ is algebraic its transcendence basis is empty, so this says $L/\mathbf Q$ is separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-normal-separable-integral-closure-finite] the integral closure of $\mathbf Z$ in $L$ is a finitely generated $\mathbf Z$-module. So $\mathbf Z$ is N-2. Hence $\mathbf Z$ is Noetherian and every $\mathbf Z/\mathfrak p$ is N-2: $\mathbf Z$ is a Nagata ring.

source.place: Algebra, Proposition Tag 0335 (proposition-ubiquity-nagata), item (3) and its proof ('check if R/p is N-2 for every prime ... clear whenever R/p is a field ... for p = (0) Lemma 032M kicks in'); Lemma Tag 032M (lemma-domain-char-zero-N-1-2), whose proof is Lemma Tag 032L

proof.text: *$A$ is N-2.* By hypothesis $\mathbf Z\to A$ is a ring map of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] and $A$ is a domain. By step 1 $\mathbf Z$ is a Nagata ring, so by Nagata's theorem [lem-weil-pbc-nagata-universally-japanese] $\mathbf Z$ is universally Japanese [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring], and therefore $A$ is N-2 [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain].

proof.text: *Conclusion.* Apply the definition of N-2 [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain] to the trivial finite extension $L=K$ of the fraction field $K$ of $A$: the integral closure $A'$ of $A$ in $K$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] is a finitely generated $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] (an N-2 domain is N-1).

split_report.summary: Mathlib has no Nagata / Japanese ring theory and no finiteness of the normalization of a domain of finite type over Z (or over a field); the only finiteness of integral closure is IsIntegralClosure.finite (Noetherian integrally closed base, finite separable extension). So the item is split along the Stacks route of its source, Proposition 0335 (3),(5): step 1 proves Z is a Nagata ring as in the proof of 0335 (F_p fields trivially N-2; Z normal Noetherian of characteristic 0, so N-2 by 032M/032L, the latter a new Mathlib leaf IsIntegralClosure.finite, separability from the existing leaf lem-weil-pbc-char-zero-field-extension-separable); step 2 applies Nagata's theorem 0334 (1)=>(3) (new unsplit node lem-weil-pbc-nagata-universally-japanese, the hard part: analytically unramified local rings) to get A N-2; step 3 takes L = K. Statement unchanged in content; stmt_deps were empty and now cite the new leaf definitions def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra (Algebra.FiniteType) and def-weil-pbc-integral-closure (integralClosure), and def-weil-finitely-generated-module. New definitions def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain (032F, N-1/N-2) and def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring (032R) are unsplit (no Mathlib counterpart). A direct route via Noether normalization was considered and rejected: over Z it only works after inverting an integer, and the points of mixed characteristic need exactly the Nagata machinery.
